//: Reference settings.json — injection & egress hardening (Policy 10/11). Native-first.
//order: Prefer the OS-sandbox egress allowlist over the Bash denylist: it breaks the trifecta egress leg for ALL commands, not just curl/wget. The hooks cover the two gaps native features leave: pipe-to-shell when the sandbox is off, and invisible-char smuggling in fetched content.
//sandbox: strictAllowlist denies any unlisted domain instead of prompting (managed settings only). This is the deterministic egress leg-break — the single strongest control here.
//permissions: Deny wins over allow. WebFetch scoped to an allowlist; fetchers kept off auto-approve as a belt-and-suspenders fallback for when the sandbox is disabled.
//mcp: Lock the set of MCP servers so a poisoned/renamed server can't be silently added. managed-mcp.json (OS path) gives exclusive control; allowManagedMcpServersOnly locks the allowlist to managed scope. Native has NO tool-description drift detection — that's the SessionStart-hash gap noted in enforcement.md.
//managed: In managed (MDM) settings, lock the rules so user/project scopes can't relax them (disableBypassPermissionsMode lives inside permissions, above).
//hooks: Copy both scripts to ~/.claude/hooks/. PreToolUse blocks pipe-to-shell forms globs can't express (fallback when sandbox off). PostToolUse strips invisible-char injection vectors from fetched content — the one indirect-injection gap Claude Code's WebFetch isolation does NOT cover.
